name: Nerepis River
text: The Nerepis River is a river approximately 25 miles (40 km) long in New Brunswick, Canada. "Na,li'pits" is Wolastoqiyik for "valley between hills" a name believed to be at least 11,000 years old by the local natives and evidenced by a fluted point discovered by archaeologists. [7] First recorded in the early 1600s by French explorer Samuel de Champlain. A popular river for canoeists and anglers, it is a tributary of the Saint John River.

depictions.name: Nerepis
depictions.text: Nerepis, New Brunswick Nerepis is a rural community in New Brunswick, Canada. During the mid-18th century, it was the site of a sizable outpost occupied by French forces, located near the coast. The edges of the settlement remained largely untouched by civilization, being the hunting grounds of Canadian lynxes.
